runs.text: The equity cushion under the debt is eroding even as debt falls. Over nine months 2026 common equity fell by USD 850 million to USD 4,999 million, net asset value per share fell from USD 20.89 to USD 18.28, and realised and unrealised losses of USD 766 million outran net investment income of USD 366 million, while debt principal fell 16.8% to USD 6,337 million. Because the debt reduction came from asset sales and repayments rather than retained earnings, debt principal to common equity eased only from 130.3% to 126.8%, so creditors still depend on portfolio marks to hold the cushion. [Documentary Fact; CP-1 Financials and credit metrics and Calculations]

Liquidity is adequate for the next two years but the later wall is larger. The issuer holds USD 111 million of cash and USD 3,197 million of availability, subject to a borrowing base that is not printed, which is 3.68 times the USD 900 million of notes due in January and July 2027 and 2.14 times unfunded commitments of USD 1,545.4 million. No committed facility expires within twelve months. Maturities then rise to USD 1,000 million in 2029, USD 1,644 million in 2030 and USD 1,300 million in 2031, USD 3,944 million in total or 62.2% of principal debt, and the 7.500% coupon on the USD 900 million of 2031 notes issued on June 8, 2026 compares with 3.400% on the notes that reached maturity in January 2026, so refinancing will cost more. [Documentary Fact for the schedule; Analyst Interpretation for the wall; CP-1 debt maturities; CP-1A transaction summary]

The nearest covenant constraint is the equity floor, not the leverage ratio. On May 8, 2026 lenders agreed to cut revolver commitments to about USD 4,051.7 million from USD 4,700.0 million, raise margins and reset the minimum shareholders' equity floor to USD 3,750.0 million from about USD 5,048.6 million. Common equity of USD 4,999 million is USD 1,249.0 million, or 25.0%, above the new floor on a proxy basis, which equals a fall of about 11.0% in investment fair value; asset coverage would take roughly a 15% to 16% fall in its base to reach 150%. Equity at 2026-09-30 was USD 49.6 million below the former floor, so, on this proxy, the amendment avoided a breach. The credit agreement's definition of equity is not supplied, so this ordering is an interpretation. [Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 Covenants and headroom]

Earnings no longer cover the shareholder distribution without sponsor support. Investment income fell 21.2% in Q3 2026 against Q3 2025 and net investment income was USD 127 million, after a USD 12 million incentive fee waiver that runs to the quarter ending March 31, 2027 with no recoupment. Net investment income covered 105.0% of Q3 common distributions of USD 121 million with the waiver and 95.0% without it, and 98.1% over nine months, while a special distribution of USD 0.20 per share and a regular USD 0.44 were declared for the fourth quarter. When the waiver ends, the same income would leave distributions about USD 12 million a quarter less covered, so either the distribution, the portfolio size or net asset value must give; each reduces the cushion or the cash available to reduce debt. [Documentary Fact for the figures; Analyst Interpretation for the consequence; CP-1 Earnings and income quality; CP-1A fee waiver row]

The debt structure puts the unsecured notes behind secured claims that can grow. The issuer has USD 4,650 million of unsecured notes against USD 1,687 million of secured debt, 73.4% and 26.6% of principal debt. The revolver is secured on substantially all assets of the Company and certain subsidiaries and has USD 3,134 million of availability, so secured borrowing ahead of the notes can rise subject to the borrowing base and the 150% asset coverage test; the 7.500% notes state they rank effectively junior to secured debt and are structurally junior to subsidiary debt. As a balance sheet mechanic and not a recovery estimate, investments at fair value less secured debt are 2.07 times the unsecured notes today. The joint venture, worth 32.7% of common equity, also carries USD 2,330.9 million of its own debt that ranks ahead of the issuer in its assets. [Documentary Fact for the structure; Analyst Interpretation for the mechanics; CP-1 Debt schedule; CP-1A Company and operating model]

Sponsor support is real but small against the decline, and governance carries open items. A KKR affiliate paid USD 150 million for convertible preferred stock that ranks junior to debt, a KKR subsidiary ran a tender offer, and the adviser waived half its subordinated income incentive fee, but the USD 150 million is 17.6% of the USD 850 million fall in equity and the preferred carries two board seats, a change-of-control put and a holder put after six years. Share repurchases of USD 90 million through October 30, 2026 use the same cash that could reduce debt. Five stockholder suits allege misleading statements on valuations and distributions, two challenge adviser fees, and the Company states it cannot estimate a loss. No priming, uptiering, collateral release or non-pro-rata exchange is documented, but the executed agreements are not supplied, so legal capacity for such steps is not assessed. [Documentary Fact for the actions; Analyst Interpretation for the weighting; CP-1A governance, ownership and conflicts rows]

The Adviser "has agreed to waive 50% of the subordinated income incentive fee" for each quarter from June 30, 2026 to March 31, 2027, with no recoupment; 12 waived in Q3 2026 and 23 over nine months

Secured revolver, a secured special-purpose facility, two consolidated CLO financings, unsecured notes and convertible preferred, bound by a 150% asset coverage requirement

runs.text: Strengths. Liquidity and maturity profile: USD 3,308 million of cash plus availability, no committed facility expiring within twelve months and USD 900 million due in 2027, so near-term debt service and refinancing are covered unless the borrowing base falls sharply. [Documentary Fact; CP-1 liquidity and maturities]. Loan book quality and seniority: 63.2% senior secured across 234 portfolio companies, top ten exposure of 21%, a 10.0% yield on accruing debt and non-accruals down from 4.2% to 3.4% of fair value since March 31, 2026, which supports interest income and marks. [Documentary Fact; CP-1A Company and operating model; CP-1 Financials]. Statutory and covenant headroom with lender support: asset coverage of 179% on debt against a 150% minimum, a lender-agreed lower equity floor and compliance reported at 2026-09-30, which show lenders willing to adjust terms rather than restrict the facility. [Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation for the lender reading; CP-1 Covenants]. Sponsor alignment: preferred capital, a tender, a four-quarter fee waiver with no recoupment and an adviser jointly run by KKR Credit and Future Standard give creditors an engaged sponsor, though the support is limited in size. [Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation; CP-1A governance rows]. Rate balance: a 100 basis point rise adds USD 27 million to twelve-month net interest income and a fall removes the same, with USD 2,600 million of fixed-rate notes swapped to floating, so rate moves do not threaten debt service on their own. [Documentary Fact; CP-1 debt schedule and earnings notes].

Weaknesses. Shrinking cushion and income: net asset value per share is down 12.5% over nine months, investment income is down 24.2%, and debt principal is still 126.8% of common equity, so the earnings base and the cushion both shrink together. [Documentary Fact; CP-1 Calculations]. Distribution not covered without help: net investment income covered 98.1% of nine-month common distributions and would cover 95.0% in Q3 without the waiver, which ends after the quarter ending March 31, 2027; a special distribution and share repurchases continue. [Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 and CP-1A]. Equity-based covenant is the nearest limit: the USD 3,750.0 million floor is about 11.0% of investment fair value from current equity and its definition is not supplied. [Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 Covenants]. Concentration in affiliated and structured holdings: the joint venture is 32.7% of common equity with USD 2,330.9 million of its own debt, asset based finance is 11.6% and equity and other 9.9% of fair value, and affiliated dividend income was USD 84 million of Q3 income of USD 294 million. [Documentary Fact; CP-1A Company and operating model]. Unsecured ranking and growing secured capacity: USD 4,650 million of notes rank effectively junior to USD 1,687 million of secured debt plus up to USD 3,134 million of revolver availability. [Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 Debt schedule]. Legal and valuation scrutiny: five suits about valuations and distributions with no loss estimate, in a business where reported net asset value drives every test. [Documentary Fact; CP-1A Claims and governance rows]. Disclosure limits: no ratings, no common stock ownership table, no covenant certificate and no quantified target leverage, so monitoring relies on management statements. [Insufficient Information; CP-0 and CP-1A gaps].

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: On May 11, 2026 the Company announced, with its first quarter results, four actions it called strategic value enhancement actions: a 150 cumulative convertible perpetual preferred investment by a KKR subsidiary, a fixed price tender offer by a KKR subsidiary for up to 150 of common stock at 11.00 per share, a 300 share repurchase program, and a waiver of 50% of the subordinated income incentive fee for four consecutive quarters (Q1 release pages 2 and 3). The preferred closed on June 29, 2026 with 6,000,000 shares sold at 25.00 to KKR Alternative Assets L.P. under a purchase agreement dated May 10, 2026 (10-Q Q3 2026 page:74), paying 5.00% in cash or, at the Company's option, 7.00% in kind, rising by 1.00% a year after 5.5 years, with a conversion price of 18.83, the March 31, 2026 net asset value per share. It ranks senior to common stock and, per the release, "junior to all existing indebtedness"; the Company may redeem it in cash at any time with board approval, holders may convert after six months and may require cash redemption at par after six years on 90 days' notice, and a majority of holders can require redemption on a change of control (10-Q Q3 2026 pages 81 to 83). The Company states it will use the proceeds for general corporate purposes including repurchases or debt repayment (10-Q Q2 2026 page:158). The Q2 release says the tender offer "was successfully completed", the preferred closed and the repurchase program commenced (Q2 release page:2); the number of shares KKR acquired in the tender and its resulting ownership are not supplied. Status of the package at 2026-09-30 is therefore closed for the preferred and tender, ongoing for the repurchase program (6,533,672 shares for 73 through September 30, plus 1,546,162 shares for 17 in October) and running for the fee waiver, which has no recoupment (10-Q Q3 2026 pages 75, 77 and 123).

New and changed debt in the period are as follows. The Senior Secured Revolving Credit Facility was amended on May 8, 2026 (Amendment No. 1, reported as a Q1 subsequent event) to cut total commitments to about 4,051.7 from 4,700.0, to raise the applicable margins for extending lenders by 0.125 percentage points in each pricing tier, and to reset the minimum shareholders' equity floor to 3,750.0 from about 5,048.6 (10-Q Q1 2026 page:107; 10-Q Q2 2026 page:108). On June 8, 2026 the Company issued 900 of 7.500% Notes due August 1, 2031 under a Sixteenth Supplemental Indenture to the 2014 base indenture, with the trustee U.S. Bank Trust Company, National Association; the notes are general unsecured obligations that "rank effectively junior to any of the Company’s secured indebtedness" and are structurally junior to subsidiary debt, carry covenants requiring compliance with the statutory asset coverage requirement, and give holders a change of control repurchase offer at 100% of principal (10-Q Q2 2026 pages 108 and 109). A swap of 900 notional to floating was entered at issuance (10-Q Q2 2026 page:95). The coupon is well above the 3.400% of the notes that reached their listed maturity of January 15, 2026; the use of proceeds of the new notes is not stated in the sources read, though the Q2 filing shows lower revolver borrowings in the same quarter. On June 29, 2026 the Meadowbrook Run and CCT Tokyo Funding secured facilities were terminated with realised losses of 2 and 0 respectively (10-Q Q2 2026 page:109). Earlier new debt that remains outstanding is the Callowhill facility (June 2, 2025, up to 400), the CLO-2 financing of 380 (March 28, 2025) and the CLO-3 financing of 389.5 closed December 18, 2025 (10-K pages 266, 277 and 278). Subsequent to the quarter and before the as-of date, the board on October 7, 2026 declared a regular distribution of 0.44 and a special distribution of 0.20 per share, and on October 28, 2026 a preferred dividend of 0.3125 per share (10-Q Q3 2026 page:123); the special distribution is described as a portion of estimated accumulated spillback income (Q3 release page:2). No further debt issue, amendment or refinancing after September 30, 2026 appears in the sources up to the cutoff.

fields.value: The effective source set is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS for all four selected consumers. The filed 10-K and three filed 10-Qs carry the statements, the note on financing arrangements, liquidity discussion, commitments, financial highlights and subsequent events for the issuer's own consolidated perimeter, and three earnings releases add attributed management narrative and the 2026 capital actions. Nothing blocks a consumer on identity, period or perimeter. The limitations are bounded: no executed financing documents, no ratings or market quotes, no investor presentations, and a business development company structure that changes which credit metrics exist. Readiness here is source sufficiency only; it does not say that any downstream analysis is complete or that any figure has been normalised or reconciled.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - **Entity and perimeter.** The registrant is a single legal entity filing consolidated statements. Note 1 describes it as an "externally managed, non-diversified, closed-end management investment company" with "various wholly-owned subsidiaries, including special-purpose financing subsidiaries" (10-Q Q3 2026 page:67). The adviser is FS/KKR Advisor, LLC (10-K FY2025 page:4: "We are managed by FS/KKR Advisor, LLC"). Borrowings of the financing subsidiaries count as the Company's: "Borrowings of each of the Company’s wholly-owned, special-purpose financing subsidiaries are considered borrowings of the Company" (10-Q Q3 2026 page:113). No separate issuer, guarantor or restricted/unrestricted group is named in the sources read; the notes and credit-facility names (Callowhill, Senior Secured Revolving Credit Facility, CLO-2, CLO-3) are borrowing vehicles inside the consolidated perimeter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - **Original authority.** The 10-K and 10-Qs are filed statements and control their facts. The three earnings releases are management presentations of the same quarters and carry non-GAAP measures (adjusted net investment income, net debt); they are attributed supporting claims and cannot override the filings. Where the release and the 10-Q show the same item they agree on the points sampled (net asset value per share $18.28 and total assets $11,695 in both the Q3 release pages 8 and 9 and the Q3 10-Q pages 2 and 3).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - **Periods and basis.** Current period Q3 2026 is covered by the Q3 10-Q (three and nine months ended September 30, 2026) and the Q3 release. The prior period FY2025 is covered by the 10-K and by the December 31, 2025 comparative column in each 2026 10-Q (for example 10-Q Q3 2026 page:2, "Total assets $ 11,695 $ 13,729"). The Q1 and Q2 10-Qs and releases provide the intermediate quarters for a discrete Q1, Q2, Q3 view; the Q2 10-Q gives six-month and the Q3 10-Q nine-month cumulative columns, so quarter versus year-to-date must stay labelled. All amounts are USD millions unless marked; the senior revolver also holds euro, sterling and Australian dollar borrowings translated to USD (10-Q Q3 2026 page:110, footnote 4).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - **Version relationships.** Each filing is the original for its period. No amendments (10-K/A, 10-Q/A) are in the pack. The pack does not hold any executed indenture, credit agreement, purchase agreement or supplement, so no base-versus-amendment question arises.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - **Debt and liquidity evidence located.** Note 9 lists every financing arrangement with rate, amount outstanding, amount available and maturity, and gives the total: "Total $ 6,487 $ 3,197" including the $150 convertible preferred (10-Q Q3 2026 page:110). The senior revolver availability is stated net of standby letters of credit: "As of September 30, 2026, $50 of such letters of credit have been issued" (page:110). A December 31, 2025 table is on page:111. The 10-K carries the full note (10-K FY2025 page:259 onward, with the indenture descriptions on pages 274 to 276). Liquidity text, unfunded commitments and the asset coverage discussion are on 10-Q Q3 2026 pages 141 to 143; the 10-K equivalent is on page:144.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - **Covenant evidence located.** The only compliance statement is generic: "The Company was in compliance with all covenants required by its financing arrangements as of September 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025" (10-Q Q3 2026 page:113). The 10-K says the covenants "require us and our subsidiaries to, among other things, maintain certain financial ratios, including asset coverage and minimum stockholders’ equity" (10-K FY2025 page:93) without printing a threshold. The statutory asset coverage test is quantified in the 10-Q: coverage on senior securities representing indebtedness of 179% and on senior securities that are stock of 177%, against a 150% requirement (page:109 and pages 142 to 143).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - **Subsequent events and the cutoff.** All seven sources were filed on or before 2026-11-05, so nothing postdates the cutoff. The Q3 10-Q and Q3 release were filed on the as-of date itself. Subsequent events are in the 10-Q Q3 2026 Note 13 (page:123) and release page:2: repurchases from October 1 through October 30, 2026, a declared fourth quarter distribution, a declared special distribution and a declared preferred dividend. Future payment dates in those items are declared terms, not events after the cutoff.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - **Transaction and ownership evidence.** The 2026 capital actions are documented: the May release announces a $150 million convertible preferred from a KKR subsidiary, a $150 million tender offer, a $300 million repurchase program and a 50% incentive fee waiver (EX-99.1 Q1 2026 pages 2 and 3); the Q3 10-Q share transactions note records the preferred issue on June 29, 2026 to KKR Alternative Assets L.P. (page:74) and the $900 principal 7.500% Notes due 2031 issued June 8, 2026 appear in the Q2 10-Q (page:95) and the Q3 note table. Governing documents (purchase agreement, advisory agreement) are referenced but not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - **Joint venture.** Credit Opportunities Partners JV, LLC is a 50/50 voting joint venture with South Carolina Retirement Systems Group Trust; the 10-Q gives selected balance sheet and income data (10-Q Q3 2026 page:94), including the joint venture's own debt, which is not the issuer's borrowing. The venture's full statements are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - **Cash basis changed.** The Q2 release nets "Cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash and foreign currency $ (109 )" in net debt (EX-99.1 Q2 2026 page:10), with restricted cash defined as "cash collateral required to be posted pursuant to the Company’s derivative contracts" (page:12). The Q3 release nets "Cash, cash equivalents, and foreign currency ($111)" (EX-99.1 Q3 2026 page:9), while the Q3 balance sheet shows "Restricted cash 61" separately (10-Q Q3 2026 page:2). The Q3 cash flow statement ends at "$ 172" including "restricted cash of $61" (page:5). The reported net debt-to-equity ratios (122% for Q2, 125% for Q3) are therefore not on an identical cash basis. Downstream modules must label which cash they use; CP-0 does not restate.

fields.name: Quote

Footnote 7 on page:110 identifies hedge-accounting carrying adjustments on four notes. The differences are of basis (carrying versus principal versus including preferred); CP-0 does not reconcile them, and CP-1 must carry the basis with each figure.

fields.name: Quote

These are different bases and periods, not a conflict in the filing.

fields.value: The business is a closed-end, externally managed business development company that lends mainly to private U.S. middle-market companies and is run by an adviser jointly operated by KKR Credit and an affiliate of Future Standard. Its creditors therefore face an asset manager's fee-and-distribution model rather than an operating company: income is investment income, the adviser is paid on gross assets and on income above a hurdle, and equity holders expect a quarterly distribution that the regulated investment company rules also require in substance. The 2026 transaction set is a package announced on May 11, 2026: a convertible preferred issue of 150 to a KKR affiliate, a tender offer by a KKR subsidiary, a 300 repurchase authorization and a 50% incentive fee waiver for four quarters, alongside a revolver amendment dated May 8, 2026, an issue of 900 of 7.500% unsecured notes on June 8, 2026 and the termination of two secured facilities on June 29, 2026. The documented behaviour is mixed rather than adverse: sponsor capital and a fee waiver are supportive, share repurchases and special distributions draw on the same cash that could reduce debt, and no priming, collateral release or non-pro-rata exchange appears in the sources. Five stockholder suits filed from May 4, 2026 allege misstatements about valuations, restructuring and the distribution strategy, which links governance to the quality of reported net asset value that supports the asset coverage and equity floor tests. The main limits are that ownership of common stock, the executed purchase and advisory agreements and the use of proceeds of the new notes are not in the pack.

fields.value: On May 11, 2026 the Company announced, with its first quarter results, four actions it called strategic value enhancement actions: a 150 cumulative convertible perpetual preferred investment by a KKR subsidiary, a fixed price tender offer by a KKR subsidiary for up to 150 of common stock at 11.00 per share, a 300 share repurchase program, and a waiver of 50% of the subordinated income incentive fee for four consecutive quarters (Q1 release pages 2 and 3). The preferred closed on June 29, 2026 with 6,000,000 shares sold at 25.00 to KKR Alternative Assets L.P. under a purchase agreement dated May 10, 2026 (10-Q Q3 2026 page:74), paying 5.00% in cash or, at the Company's option, 7.00% in kind, rising by 1.00% a year after 5.5 years, with a conversion price of 18.83, the March 31, 2026 net asset value per share. It ranks senior to common stock and, per the release, "junior to all existing indebtedness"; the Company may redeem it in cash at any time with board approval, holders may convert after six months and may require cash redemption at par after six years on 90 days' notice, and a majority of holders can require redemption on a change of control (10-Q Q3 2026 pages 81 to 83). The Company states it will use the proceeds for general corporate purposes including repurchases or debt repayment (10-Q Q2 2026 page:158). The Q2 release says the tender offer "was successfully completed", the preferred closed and the repurchase program commenced (Q2 release page:2); the number of shares KKR acquired in the tender and its resulting ownership are not supplied. Status of the package at 2026-09-30 is therefore closed for the preferred and tender, ongoing for the repurchase program (6,533,672 shares for 73 through September 30, plus 1,546,162 shares for 17 in October) and running for the fee waiver, which has no recoupment (10-Q Q3 2026 pages 75, 77 and 123).

On June 8, 2026 the Company issued 900 of 7.500% Notes due August 1, 2031 under a Sixteenth Supplemental Indenture to the 2014 base indenture, with the trustee U.S. Bank Trust Company, National Association; the notes are general unsecured obligations that "rank effectively junior to any of the Company’s secured indebtedness" and are structurally junior to subsidiary debt, carry covenants requiring compliance with the statutory asset coverage requirement, and give holders a change of control repurchase offer at 100% of principal (10-Q Q2 2026 pages 108 and 109). A swap of 900 notional to floating was entered at issuance (10-Q Q2 2026 page:95). The coupon is well above the 3.400% of the notes that reached their listed maturity of January 15, 2026; the use of proceeds of the new notes is not stated in the sources read, though the Q2 filing shows lower revolver borrowings in the same quarter. On June 29, 2026 the Meadowbrook Run and CCT Tokyo Funding secured facilities were terminated with realised losses of 2 and 0 respectively (10-Q Q2 2026 page:109). Earlier new debt that remains outstanding is the Callowhill facility (June 2, 2025, up to 400), the CLO-2 financing of 380 (March 28, 2025) and the CLO-3 financing of 389.5 closed December 18, 2025 (10-K pages 266, 277 and 278). Subsequent to the quarter and before the as-of date, the board on October 7, 2026 declared a regular distribution of 0.44 and a special distribution of 0.20 per share, and on October 28, 2026 a preferred dividend of 0.3125 per share (10-Q Q3 2026 page:123); the special distribution is described as a portion of estimated accumulated spillback income (Q3 release page:2). No further debt issue, amendment or refinancing after September 30, 2026 appears in the sources up to the cutoff.

fields.value: FS KKR Capital Corp's creditors are adequately protected in the near term, but the credit is weakening because the equity value beneath the debt is shrinking. The strongest support is liquidity of USD 3,308 million against USD 900 million of notes maturing in 2027, asset coverage of 179% on debt against the 150% minimum, and a lender-agreed lower equity floor of USD 3,750.0 million. The weakest point is the fall in net asset value per share from USD 20.89 to USD 18.28 over nine months 2026, with investment income down 24.2% as the portfolio shrinks, distributions above net investment income and five stockholder suits with no loss estimate. What decides the outcome is whether portfolio marks stabilise and non-accruals, at 3.4% of fair value, keep falling, because the covenants and the asset coverage test all run off net asset value. [Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 figures; CP-1A governance and litigation rows]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The equity cushion under the debt is eroding even as debt falls. Over nine months 2026 common equity fell by USD 850 million to USD 4,999 million, net asset value per share fell from USD 20.89 to USD 18.28, and realised and unrealised losses of USD 766 million outran net investment income of USD 366 million, while debt principal fell 16.8% to USD 6,337 million. Because the debt reduction came from asset sales and repayments rather than retained earnings, debt principal to common equity eased only from 130.3% to 126.8%, so creditors still depend on portfolio marks to hold the cushion. [Documentary Fact; CP-1 Financials and credit metrics and Calculations]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate for the next two years but the later wall is larger. The issuer holds USD 111 million of cash and USD 3,197 million of availability, subject to a borrowing base that is not printed, which is 3.68 times the USD 900 million of notes due in January and July 2027 and 2.14 times unfunded commitments of USD 1,545.4 million. No committed facility expires within twelve months. Maturities then rise to USD 1,000 million in 2029, USD 1,644 million in 2030 and USD 1,300 million in 2031, USD 3,944 million in total or 62.2% of principal debt, and the 7.500% coupon on the USD 900 million of 2031 notes issued on June 8, 2026 compares with 3.400% on the notes that reached maturity in January 2026, so refinancing will cost more. [Documentary Fact for the schedule; Analyst Interpretation for the wall; CP-1 debt maturities; CP-1A transaction summary]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The nearest covenant constraint is the equity floor, not the leverage ratio. On May 8, 2026 lenders agreed to cut revolver commitments to about USD 4,051.7 million from USD 4,700.0 million, raise margins and reset the minimum shareholders' equity floor to USD 3,750.0 million from about USD 5,048.6 million. Common equity of USD 4,999 million is USD 1,249.0 million, or 25.0%, above the new floor on a proxy basis, which equals a fall of about 11.0% in investment fair value; asset coverage would take roughly a 15% to 16% fall in its base to reach 150%. Equity at 2026-09-30 was USD 49.6 million below the former floor, so, on this proxy, the amendment avoided a breach. The credit agreement's definition of equity is not supplied, so this ordering is an interpretation. [Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 Covenants and headroom]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings no longer cover the shareholder distribution without sponsor support. Investment income fell 21.2% in Q3 2026 against Q3 2025 and net investment income was USD 127 million, after a USD 12 million incentive fee waiver that runs to the quarter ending March 31, 2027 with no recoupment. Net investment income covered 105.0% of Q3 common distributions of USD 121 million with the waiver and 95.0% without it, and 98.1% over nine months, while a special distribution of USD 0.20 per share and a regular USD 0.44 were declared for the fourth quarter. When the waiver ends, the same income would leave distributions about USD 12 million a quarter less covered, so either the distribution, the portfolio size or net asset value must give; each reduces the cushion or the cash available to reduce debt. [Documentary Fact for the figures; Analyst Interpretation for the consequence; CP-1 Earnings and income quality; CP-1A fee waiver row]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The debt structure puts the unsecured notes behind secured claims that can grow. The issuer has USD 4,650 million of unsecured notes against USD 1,687 million of secured debt, 73.4% and 26.6% of principal debt. The revolver is secured on substantially all assets of the Company and certain subsidiaries and has USD 3,134 million of availability, so secured borrowing ahead of the notes can rise subject to the borrowing base and the 150% asset coverage test; the 7.500% notes state they rank effectively junior to secured debt and are structurally junior to subsidiary debt. As a balance sheet mechanic and not a recovery estimate, investments at fair value less secured debt are 2.07 times the unsecured notes today. The joint venture, worth 32.7% of common equity, also carries USD 2,330.9 million of its own debt that ranks ahead of the issuer in its assets. [Documentary Fact for the structure; Analyst Interpretation for the mechanics; CP-1 Debt schedule; CP-1A Company and operating model]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor support is real but small against the decline, and governance carries open items. A KKR affiliate paid USD 150 million for convertible preferred stock that ranks junior to debt, a KKR subsidiary ran a tender offer, and the adviser waived half its subordinated income incentive fee, but the USD 150 million is 17.6% of the USD 850 million fall in equity and the preferred carries two board seats, a change-of-control put and a holder put after six years. Share repurchases of USD 90 million through October 30, 2026 use the same cash that could reduce debt. Five stockholder suits allege misleading statements on valuations and distributions, two challenge adviser fees, and the Company states it cannot estimate a loss. No priming, uptiering, collateral release or non-pro-rata exchange is documented, but the executed agreements are not supplied, so legal capacity for such steps is not assessed. [Documentary Fact for the actions; Analyst Interpretation for the weighting; CP-1A governance, ownership and conflicts rows]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. Liquidity and maturity profile: USD 3,308 million of cash plus availability, no committed facility expiring within twelve months and USD 900 million due in 2027, so near-term debt service and refinancing are covered unless the borrowing base falls sharply. [Documentary Fact; CP-1 liquidity and maturities]. Loan book quality and seniority: 63.2% senior secured across 234 portfolio companies, top ten exposure of 21%, a 10.0% yield on accruing debt and non-accruals down from 4.2% to 3.4% of fair value since March 31, 2026, which supports interest income and marks. [Documentary Fact; CP-1A Company and operating model; CP-1 Financials]. Statutory and covenant headroom with lender support: asset coverage of 179% on debt against a 150% minimum, a lender-agreed lower equity floor and compliance reported at 2026-09-30, which show lenders willing to adjust terms rather than restrict the facility. [Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation for the lender reading; CP-1 Covenants]. Sponsor alignment: preferred capital, a tender, a four-quarter fee waiver with no recoupment and an adviser jointly run by KKR Credit and Future Standard give creditors an engaged sponsor, though the support is limited in size. [Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation; CP-1A governance rows]. Rate balance: a 100 basis point rise adds USD 27 million to twelve-month net interest income and a fall removes the same, with USD 2,600 million of fixed-rate notes swapped to floating, so rate moves do not threaten debt service on their own. [Documentary Fact; CP-1 debt schedule and earnings notes].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Shrinking cushion and income: net asset value per share is down 12.5% over nine months, investment income is down 24.2%, and debt principal is still 126.8% of common equity, so the earnings base and the cushion both shrink together. [Documentary Fact; CP-1 Calculations]. Distribution not covered without help: net investment income covered 98.1% of nine-month common distributions and would cover 95.0% in Q3 without the waiver, which ends after the quarter ending March 31, 2027; a special distribution and share repurchases continue. [Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 and CP-1A]. Equity-based covenant is the nearest limit: the USD 3,750.0 million floor is about 11.0% of investment fair value from current equity and its definition is not supplied. [Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 Covenants]. Concentration in affiliated and structured holdings: the joint venture is 32.7% of common equity with USD 2,330.9 million of its own debt, asset based finance is 11.6% and equity and other 9.9% of fair value, and affiliated dividend income was USD 84 million of Q3 income of USD 294 million. [Documentary Fact; CP-1A Company and operating model]. Unsecured ranking and growing secured capacity: USD 4,650 million of notes rank effectively junior to USD 1,687 million of secured debt plus up to USD 3,134 million of revolver availability. [Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 Debt schedule]. Legal and valuation scrutiny: five suits about valuations and distributions with no loss estimate, in a business where reported net asset value drives every test. [Documentary Fact; CP-1A Claims and governance rows]. Disclosure limits: no ratings, no common stock ownership table, no covenant certificate and no quantified target leverage, so monitoring relies on management statements. [Insufficient Information; CP-0 and CP-1A gaps].
